standard_prerequisites.name: The gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t), its objects, and the canonical functor Can

standard_prerequisites.name: The zeroth cohomology functor H^0 on the gluing category
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used throughout the counted proof span
standard_prerequisites.use: Is one of the two functors, and its value on glued objects is what the comparison map targets.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of direct sums and cokernels in the gluing category and exactness properties of Can
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what extends the adjunction comparison from N = R to arbitrary N.

core_obligations: Let bold M = (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) be an object of the gluing category, and for an R-module N exhibit the map from Hom(Can(N), bold M) to Hom_R(N, H^0(bold M)) sending psi to H^0(psi) composed with the obvious map N -> H^0(Can(N)) (proof lines 24709-24718).
Observe that by construction this map is an isomorphism for N = R, noting that R -> H^0(Can(R)) need not be an isomorphism in general (proof lines 24719-24720).
Record that the gluing category has direct sums and cokernels, and that Can commutes with direct sums and cokernels (proof lines 24721-24723).
Conclude that the displayed map is bijective for every N by writing N as a cokernel of a map between free R-modules; the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 24723-24725).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that in the gluing setup the functor H^0 from the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) to R-modules is right adjoint to the canonical functor Can in the other direction (source lines 24701-24707). The proof constructs the adjunction comparison map explicitly: for an object bold M = (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) of the gluing category and an R-module N, the proof exhibits the map from Hom(Can(N), bold M) to Hom_R(N, H^0(bold M)) sending psi to H^0(psi) composed with the obvious map N -> H^0(Can(N)) (proof lines 24709-24718). It then notes that by construction this map is an isomorphism for N = R, even though R -> H^0(Can(R)) need not be an isomorphism in general (proof lines 24719-24720). The substantive step extends this from N = R to all N: the proof observes that the gluing category has direct sums and cokernels, that Can commutes with direct sums and cokernels, and hence that the displayed map is bijective because N can be written as a cokernel of a map between free R-modules (proof lines 24721-24724). The author states that the details are omitted (proof line 24725). The non-routine content is the reduction from the single case N = R to all modules by presenting N as a cokernel of free modules, using the exactness properties of Can.
